brief:
A Gaza mother describes the constrained reality of raising children during the territory's conflict, venturing outside briefly with her kids to experience the street before returning indoors, according to the Electronic Intifada. The routine outing—breathing polluted air—offers little change from the confinement of home life.

The account reflects the compressed existence of Palestinian families in Gaza, where the ordinary rhythms of childhood and motherhood unfold against a backdrop of persistent insecurity and limited freedom of movement.
dek: As an exciting journey, I venture outside with my kids onto the street to smell the polluted air. We go back inside and not much has changed.
title: Gaza mother navigates daily life amid ongoing violence
